1.name: tier 1
1.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 180, saturated (every unit vector of the lattice a generator)
1.odd_girth: FS-58's odd_girth, exact to length 15 or a 400,000-point BFS cap, whichever binds first; none_up_to recorded

1b.name: tier 1b (the radius ladder)
1b.defined: 2026-09-20, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md, the owner's re-plan after phase B, ruling 2 (phase B')
1b.scope: every rank-4 lattice whose state is Open and whose tier-1 R = 1.5 ball record is `Over cap (not asked)`; a lattice whose R = 1.5 ball was asked is out of scope, and tier 1's definition is unchanged
1b.lattices: tier 1's lattices, unchanged: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 180, saturated
1b.odd_girth: tier 1's, unchanged; no lattice record is rewritten by this tier
1b.radius_rule: walk the rungs 1.2 then 1.0. A rung whose PREDICTED points (pi^2 R^4 / covolume) exceed point_cap is not asked; the first rung whose prediction fits is asked. If that rung's EXACT point count also exceeds point_cap the ladder descends to the next fitting rung -- the exact count is strictly better information than the prediction and the descent can only ask more, never fewer. If no rung's prediction fits, one `Over cap (not asked)` record is written at the first rung carrying both predictions.
1b.onset_rule: a rung that refuses is followed by the next rung down at a 120 s wall, as phase B's onset radii were, to hand phase C a smaller refusing ball; it is a bonus ask and never part of the accounting

2.name: tier 2
2.defined: 2026-09-19, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md decision B (phase E; d = 7 mod 8 fields not landed at tier 1, 167 excluded)
2.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 420, saturated
2.odd_girth: FS-58's odd_girth, exact to length 15 or a 400,000-point BFS cap, whichever binds first; none_up_to recorded

1c.name: tier 1c (the long wall)
1c.defined: 2026-09-20, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md, the owner's re-plan after phase B', ruling 3, item E.1a
1c.scope: every ball a tier-1b record left `Unknown (budget)` at a census field with no certified witness -- the SAME lattice, the SAME radius, the SAME point cap and the SAME symmetry break. Only the solver's wall changes, from 600 s to 3600 s. This tier creates no lattice record and no filter record and asks no ball nobody has asked before; its records shadow the tier-1b records they re-ask, which stay on disk as the history.
1c.not_in_scope: the tier-1 `Unknown` records -- every one of them is at a field already landed -- and the tier-1 `Unknown` records at the seven control fields, whose planes are 2- or 3-colourable by theorem: an `Unknown` is not a near-refusal.
1c.lattices: tier 1's lattices, unchanged; this tier creates no lattice record

reask.fields: census fields with no certified witness

2l.name: tier 2l (deeper lattices, the same cap)
2l.defined: 2026-09-20, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md, the owner's re-plan after phase B', ruling 3, item E.1b
2l.scope: every census field with no certified witness. Lattices to NMAX = 420 -- a superset of tier 1's NMAX = 180 set, so every tier-1 and tier-1b ball record still answers the ball it answered and is never re-asked; the new work is the finer lattices. The point cap and the solver's wall are tier 1's, deliberately: phase B' measured that at this depth the binding constraint is the solver and not the cap (24 of 37 asks ran to the 600 s wall), so this tier buys DEPTH and not SIZE, and tier 2's 3,000,000-point cap is not run.
2l.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 420, saturated (every unit vector of the lattice a generator)
2l.odd_girth: NOT computed at this tier: every 2l lattice record carries odd_girth.status `not asked`. Phase 0 measured the exact odd girth at about 900x the cost of the rest of `lattices` (1,648 CPU-s against 1.8 s at d = 11), and R-cycle is scored on tier 1's lattices, whose population is stated. A 2l lattice has no odd-girth column and must not be counted in an odd-girth table.
2l.radius_rule: every rank-4 Open lattice within this tier's NMAX walks the rungs 1.5, 1.2, 1.0: the first rung whose PREDICTED points (pi^2 R^4 / covolume) fit the point cap is asked, and a rung whose EXACT count overflows descends to the next fitting rung. If no rung's prediction fits, one `Over cap (not asked)` record is written at the first rung. Unlike tier 1b there is NO base-radius precondition, because this tier introduces lattices of its own that no earlier tier ever asked.
2l.onset_rule: a rung that refuses is followed by the next rung down at a 120 s wall, to hand phase C a smaller refusing ball; a bonus ask, never part of the accounting
